questions.text: A patient has a reduced vital capacity and the provider wants to know whether the pattern is restrictive or obstructive. Which measurement is the main target of a lung volume study?
A lab offers nitrogen washout, helium dilution, and body plethysmography. What do these three techniques have in common?

answers.text: They are methods for determining FRC
They replace the need for spirometry
They all require a forced expiratory maneuver only

questions.text: The technologist is preparing a VTG test. Which equipment setup best matches that procedure?

answers.text: A sealed body box with airway pressure measurement
A pulse oximeter and exercise treadmill
A carbon monoxide analyzer for single-breath testing

questions.text: In an open-circuit nitrogen washout, what is the purpose of having the patient breathe pure oxygen?

answers.text: To wash nitrogen out of the lungs for FRC calculation
To stabilize helium concentration in a closed circuit
To create the closed shutter needed for Boyle's law

questions.text: During nitrogen washout, the technologist sees expired N2 fall to the test endpoint before the maximum time has elapsed. What should this indicate?

answers.text: The washout criterion has been met
The shutter should be closed for panting
The helium correction should be added

questions.text: A nitrogen washout calculation includes N2 removed from blood and tissue. How should this tissue contribution be handled?

answers.text: Subtract it from the measured exhaled nitrogen volume
Add it to the measured exhaled nitrogen volume
Use it as the patient's ERV
Use it only when calculating airway resistance

questions.text: In helium dilution, the spirometer starts with a known gas volume and a helium mixture. Which starting mixture from the lesson should the technologist prepare?

answers.text: 600-800 mL spirometer volume with helium at 10%
100 mL spirometer volume with helium at 1%
30-40 mL spirometer volume with helium at 21%
A closed shutter with no added helium

questions.text: A helium dilution system is missing soda lime. Which hazard becomes most likely if the test proceeds?

answers.text: Nitrogen washout from blood and tissue
Over-reading of mouth pressure during panting

questions.text: A helium dilution result has not accounted for helium dissolving in the blood. Which correction from the lesson prevents FRC from reading too high?
A patient with emphysema has suspected trapped gas and uneven ventilation. Which FRC method is most likely to capture that trapped thoracic gas?
During panting against a closed shutter, the body box uses pressure and volume changes to calculate VTG. Which principle supports that calculation?

answers.text: At constant temperature, pressure and volume change in relation to each other
Gas diffuses according to membrane surface area
Total pressure equals the sum of partial pressures
Gas dissolved in liquid depends on solubility

questions.text: The technologist starts the VTG maneuver after normal tidal breathing rather than after a maximal inhale. What lung volume level is being targeted at the start?
Why can body plethysmography report a larger value than gas dilution methods in a patient with emphysema?

answers.text: It includes gas trapped in thoracic compartments
It subtracts oxygen demand from FRC
It measures only gas that is evenly ventilated

questions.text: Before the SVC maneuver in the body box, the patient's tidal breaths vary by more than 100 mL. What is the best interpretation?

answers.text: Baseline breathing is not stable enough for accurate ERV and IC
The nitrogen washout endpoint has been reached
The patient has demonstrated a valid Raw value
The helium correction is no longer needed

questions.text: A patient pants against an occluded airway during VTG testing. Why is airway pressure useful at that moment?

answers.text: With no flow, mouth pressure reflects alveolar pressure
With no flow, helium cannot dissolve in blood
With no flow, ERV automatically equals VC
With no flow, nitrogen remains at atmospheric concentration

questions.text: A report describes the gas left in the lungs after a normal passive exhalation. Which value is being described?
A patient's measured FRC is 3.0 L and ERV is 1.1 L. Which calculated value does this determine?
A patient has a vital capacity of 4.0 L. Based on the lesson's normal proportions, about 3.0 L would correspond to which capacity?
An ERV is reduced and vital capacity is also reduced. Which interpretation fits the relationship described in the lesson?

answers.text: ERV changes tend to parallel VC and can be reduced in restriction
ERV is unrelated to VC and only reflects airway resistance
Reduced ERV confirms hyperinflation by itself
Reduced ERV means RV cannot be calculated

questions.text: A patient exhales maximally but still has an abnormally large amount of gas left in the lungs. Which process does this most strongly suggest from the lesson?

answers.text: Loss of helium into the blood only
A low FRC with low RV

questions.text: The technologist has FRC and IC after testing. Which calculation can be made from those two values?
A patient has reduced TLC on lung volume testing. Which broad ventilatory pattern should be suspected?
A TLC result is below LLN but still above 70% predicted. How should the restriction severity be documented?
A lung volume report shows FRC above ULN while TLC remains within normal limits. Which interpretation is most consistent with the lesson?
Both FRC and TLC are above the predicted upper limit. Which term best matches this obstructive lung volume pattern?
Spirometry confirms obstruction and lung volumes show TLC below LLN. What pattern does this combination support?
A body box report shows Raw of 3.0 cmH2O/L/sec. How should this be interpreted using the lesson's cutoff?

answers.text: No reliable adult reference exists for Raw
Restrictive disease is confirmed by Raw alone

questions.text: A patient has sGaw below 0.15 L/sec/cmH2O. Which interpretation fits the lesson?

answers.text: The value is used only for nitrogen correction

questions.text: A patient's Gaw is measured at a specific VTG. Which calculation normalizes conductance for the lung volume where it was measured?
A patient has reduced TLC but normal Raw and Gaw. Which statement best fits the lesson?

answers.text: Restrictive disease can show normal resistance and conductance values
All reduced TLC patterns must have elevated Raw
Conductance values are used only during helium dilution
